nodes.label: Query analysis: why Unit 1 Teacher Guidance bridges communities
nodes.norm_label: query analysis: why unit 1 teacher guidance bridges communities
nodes.rationale: The bridge is a document-structure artifact of the OCR'd heading hierarchy, not a semantic dependency or code call. Extraction links every heading to its immediate parent with EXTRACTED conceptually_related_to edges; the H1 Unit 1 Teacher Guidance has 11 children spanning at least four communities, giving betweenness 0.678. Community detection split children into Learning Experience Activities, Integral Skills Activities and Programming and Compilation, with the rest seeding Unit 1 Topic Index. There is no design-intent rationale on the hub.

nodes.label: Catalogue<T>
nodes.rationale: all exists because declaration-order evaluation is required; getById returns undefined for missing IDs and never throws.

nodes.label: Effect-to-event mapping
nodes.rationale: One buffered event per effect guarantees every state change is explainable in the output log.

nodes.label: Canonical GameEvent union
nodes.rationale: Consolidates the seven architecture variants and thirteen subsystem variants, plus bookkeeping events, into one union.

nodes.label: Title screen overlay
nodes.rationale: v1 has a title screen as a UI overlay, not persisted state; Continue is enabled only when boot returned a valid save.

nodes.label: content:generate
nodes.rationale: Generated TypeScript is committed so the site stays fully static; AreaDefinition.roomIds and ConversationNode.topics are derived deterministically.

nodes.label: HazardCatalogue
nodes.rationale: getForRoom avoids scanning the whole content set each turn; the level-start room is the runtime startRoomId on AreaDefinition.

nodes.label: Hint context resolution order
nodes.rationale: Explicit targetId, then active quiz, then current room; if none resolves, emit a friendly no-hints-here message rather than an error.

nodes.label: HintSystem
nodes.rationale: Default scorePenalty is zero because penalties discourage behaviour a revision tool should encourage; any penalty is emitted as hint-penalty-applied for ScoreTracker.

nodes.label: Conversation flow
nodes.rationale: Conversations start implicitly on ask/give/show; there is deliberately no turn timeout, only bye or leaving the room.

nodes.label: Knowledge gating (knowsAbout / AltTopic)
nodes.rationale: learn-topic adds IDs to knownTopics; where a fact could be found independently, a second topic with a negated npc-knows condition implements the TADS AltTopic pattern.

nodes.label: TopicResolver
nodes.rationale: NameResolver cannot resolve free-text topics, so TopicResolver maps object alias, then node keyword, then free-text fallback; unknown topics never say parser error.

nodes.label: PuzzleSystem completion detection
nodes.rationale: PuzzleSystem runs in phase 4 after hazards and NPC reactions; the phase is set to solved before puzzle-solved is emitted, preventing double-firing.

nodes.label: Content registration via catalogues
nodes.rationale: Each system exposes a catalogue bundled into one injected ContentBundle; engine consumes interfaces so tests can inject small fixtures.

nodes.label: Effect
nodes.rationale: Handlers and domain systems return effects rather than writing state; every effect produces at least one buffered event.

nodes.label: EffectApplier
nodes.rationale: EffectApplier.apply is the only code that mutates GameState fields driven by effects.

nodes.label: Scheduler (fuse and daemon)
nodes.rationale: A fuse fires at zero then is removed; a daemon resets to repeatEveryTurns; all scheduled state is serialised so a reload resumes timers accurately.

nodes.label: AreaProgress
nodes.rationale: maxScore is stored only as a display fallback and is refreshed from content via SpecTopicCatalogue.getByAreaId at restore.

nodes.label: GameStateDto
nodes.rationale: Only plain strings, numbers, booleans, arrays and records enter the DTO; optional fields are omitted rather than set to undefined.

nodes.label: Per-puzzle scoring
nodes.rationale: Each solved puzzle, quiz pass and first room visit awards its own declared points within SpecTopic.maxScore; topic-completed records completion and awards nothing.

nodes.label: Quiz combat decisions resolved
nodes.rationale: No per-question timer; answer outside a quiz is friendly; fail resets position and lives only; passMark is a count; onFail change-lives is the single life-loss source.

nodes.label: Decisions content must not assume
nodes.rationale: Win condition, 3 lives, verb list, no undo/autosave/slots, save key, scoring formula, title screen, registration, boot start and validation are authoritative from architecture section 11.

nodes.label: Hazard failure consequences
nodes.rationale: Hazards are brief penalties, not puzzles: lose a life, return to level start, optionally reset level-local flags. Puzzle phase never resets and hints are never offered.

nodes.label: Adaptive hints
nodes.rationale: This is a revision tool, so helping a stuck student is part of the product; hints escalate and unlock on evidence of being stuck, but never reveal the answer.

nodes.label: Hint score interaction
nodes.rationale: HintSystem never writes score directly; it emits hint-penalty-applied and ScoreTracker, the sole score writer, applies it.

nodes.label: TADS 3 conversation model
nodes.rationale: Adapted from ActorState, TopicEntry, ConvNode and knowsAbout because it produces rich-feeling dialogue from small data tables and needs no generative model or backend.

nodes.label: Shared rule spine
nodes.rationale: NPCs, hazards, quizzes, puzzles and hints all reduce to when a condition holds, apply effects, possibly on a schedule; five separate engines would duplicate the same machinery.

nodes.label: Buffered turn pipeline
nodes.rationale: Events are buffered for the whole turn and published once after state is final: deterministic output, no half-updated UI and explicit observer order.

nodes.label: Score derived at restore
nodes.rationale: score is absent from the save; it is sum(progress[].earnedScore), with ScoreTracker as sole writer of earnedScore.

nodes.label: No schema migration in v1
nodes.rationale: SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1 while the game is unreleased; new fields are added directly and migration is revisited before public release.

nodes.label: Quarantine
nodes.rationale: On boot only a corrupt live save is copied to one never-overwritten slot with raw text, reason and timestamp; boot continues with Continue disabled and a download action.

nodes.label: Validation contract
nodes.rationale: Required keys and types are checked, extra keys ignored to permit additive v1 fields; order is JSON parse, version, shape, content references.

nodes.label: Unit 1 Teacher Guidance
nodes.rationale: Bridge is a graph-structure artifact, not a semantic dependency or code call: the extractor links every heading to its immediate parent heading with an EXTRACTED conceptually_related_to edge (confidence 1.0). The H1 Unit 1 Teacher Guidance at L95 has 11 direct children - the eight numbered sections 1.1 to 1.8, Glossary for Unit 1, Learning Experiences and Opportunities for embedding elements of the Curriculum for Wales - spanning at least four communities, giving betweenness 0.678 and making it a surprising cross-community bridge. Unit 1 Topic Index is only the label of the hub's own community; the actual bridging node is the H1 heading. SUMMARY OF AMENDMENTS (L16) and Unit 1 Assessment objectives and weightings (L89) are separate sibling H1 roots with no edge to the hub, so the hub is not the document's unique entry point. There is no teaching design intent behind the bridge.

nodes.label: Subsystem design documents
nodes.rationale: Build persistence, then content toolchain, then registry and UI shell, then hazards and puzzles, NPCs, combat and hints last.

nodes.label: Bible (content-bible.md)
nodes.rationale: Co-authored with the user; changed only with their approval; owns premise, areas, cast, topic allocation, PDG and the ID/alias registry.

nodes.label: ID and alias registry
nodes.rationale: The bible owns one registry with kebab-case kind prefixes; aliases are globally unique across objects and NPCs.

nodes.label: Content authority order
nodes.rationale: Course facts come from wjec-unit1.md and the PDF, then COVERAGE.md, then the bible; subsystem docs own data shape and runtime behaviour.

nodes.label: V4 walkthrough audit
nodes.rationale: An ordered path from startRoomId to game-won proves every gate satisfiable, every option reachable and no soft-lock; an area whose win contribution cannot be shown is not integrated.

nodes.label: Workflow gates W1-W6
nodes.rationale: No writer is launched before bible approval; validation precedes review; generation is a mechanical handoff after integration.

nodes.label: AreaDefinition
nodes.rationale: startRoomId promotes the old levelStart authoring note into a runtime field; lives reset on area change, not every room move.

nodes.label: Eight structural validation gates
nodes.rationale: content-ids, quiz-content, puzzle-graph, world-graph, hint-content, hazard-content, npc-content and score-content, shared by validate, Vitest and boot.

nodes.label: YAML authoring format
nodes.rationale: YAML is the sole authoring format; no Markdown design cards survive migration and there is no build-time or runtime YAML parsing.

nodes.label: .graphifyrc YAML-to-document remap (C0 resolved)
nodes.rationale: Plain graphify classifies .yaml as code and emits only generic key nodes, losing artefact IDs and prose; docs/.graphifyrc remaps YAML to document classification for builds rooted at docs.

nodes.label: MetaAction
nodes.rationale: Typed save/load/download/import/restart are aliases for SaveControls buttons, intercepted by Game before core dispatch, so they never enter Command or advance the turn.

nodes.label: SaveDto envelope
nodes.rationale: Adds version and savedAt from the injected Clock to GameStateDto; imports preserve the original savedAt.

nodes.label: SaveManager
nodes.rationale: Catalogues, StorageAdapter and Clock are injected so build/save/load/validate/restore can be exercised with fakes.

nodes.label: StorageAdapter
nodes.rationale: An interface only; BrowserStorage implements it so SaveManager stays testable with in-memory fakes.

nodes.label: Static-first architecture
nodes.rationale: Fully static site on GitHub Pages: no runtime server and no server-side state; localStorage is the live store and JSON is the portable store.

nodes.label: Condition
nodes.rationale: Conditions are pure and missing flags or IDs evaluate to false, never throw; the same evaluator powers pre-turn validation and post-turn reactions.

nodes.label: Action-flag requirements
nodes.rationale: Requirements must be action-set flags, not mere possession: carrying the brass key must not auto-solve the door; using it sets door-unlocked.

nodes.label: Area: The Switchyard (area-1-2-1-data-representation)
nodes.rationale: StartRoomId declared once here (D4); rooms are navigation and setting so every room declares score 0 (P6).

nodes.label: N3 Diegetic learning
nodes.rationale: GCSE concepts are mechanisms of the fictional world, not interruptions; a quiz is an in-world challenge and a puzzle a task using the concept.

nodes.label: ConversationNode
nodes.rationale: Runtime node membership is established by enter-node effects carrying actorId; node actorId in cards is authoring-only metadata.

nodes.label: ConversationTopic
nodes.rationale: Runtime ConversationTopic carries an optional actorId generated and validated in content-rules section 4.3 so topics do not leak across actors.

nodes.label: Puzzle phases
nodes.rationale: Multi-step tasks are one puzzle per step in the dependency graph; a puzzle may be activated before it is solved.

nodes.label: Puzzle Dependency Graph (PDG)
nodes.rationale: Ron Gilbert / Noah Falstein's PDG is an authoring and testing tool, not runtime machinery; a cycle means a softlock and only ancestor plot points may be referenced in prose.

nodes.label: Win condition (game-won)
nodes.rationale: Win fires when every spec topic marked covered with evidence is completed; only covered topics with evidence are scoreable.

nodes.label: Premise: AI teleports inattentive pupils inside the machine
nodes.norm_label: premise: ai teleports inattentive pupils inside the machine
nodes.rationale: Digital death is an in-fiction threat, not a mechanic: three lives reset on area change, zero lives gives lost/game-over (§8; narrative-principles §§5,8).

nodes.label: Canonical Command union
nodes.rationale: This is the single canonical union; partial lists in architecture, npcs, combat and hints documents now link here instead of duplicating it.

nodes.label: SpecTopicCatalogue
nodes.rationale: getByAreaId is what restore needs to refresh AreaProgress.maxScore.

nodes.label: SpecTopic
nodes.rationale: Mirrors docs/coverage/COVERAGE.md: topic id, spec reference, code location, status, evidence, roomIds and maxScore.

nodes.label: Reviewer rubrics (content-critic and pck-reviewer)
nodes.rationale: Both reviewers are read-only and independent; a passing validate is a precondition, not a substitute.

nodes.label: HintSequence
nodes.rationale: targets may include GCSE spec topic IDs so ScorePanel can label the revision area a hint belongs to.

nodes.label: Counters and stuckness
nodes.rationale: Keys are free-form at load; only conditions interpret hints-shown, failed-attempts and turns-since. Counters are never pruned, keeping a full audit trail.

nodes.label: Quiz attempts
nodes.rationale: quizAttempts holds lifetime starts per quiz; attemptsAllowed is checked before starting and omitted means unlimited.

nodes.label: SessionStatus
nodes.rationale: playing, won or lost is persisted; Session sets it on game-won or game-over, and restore skips the win check when it is not playing.

nodes.label: Session win-check owner
nodes.rationale: Session.observe runs in phase 5 after ScoreTracker.observe so end events carry the final score; restore derives but never re-emits an end event.

nodes.label: Adversarial quiz combat
nodes.rationale: No stat-based combat: an NPC questions the player on GCSE material. It is both a damage source and the main revision loop.

nodes.label: Seeded question order
nodes.rationale: Question order uses the seeded Random port; the seed advances on each draw and is saved in rngSeed, so no Math.random exists in core.

nodes.label: Random port
nodes.rationale: Quiz order and varied NPC replies need randomness but the core must stay deterministic for saves and tests, so a seeded PRNG port replaces Math.random.

nodes.label: Restore-time derivation
nodes.rationale: SaveManager.restore derives score and refreshes maxScore from the live catalogue; the win check uses covered topics with evidence and never emits on restore.

nodes.label: Door and container verbs
nodes.rationale: v1 gives doors and containers dedicated open/close/unlock/put verbs rather than relying solely on use; use still works for puzzles.

nodes.label: GameViewData
nodes.rationale: Transcript and transient panels read events; ScorePanel reads this state channel. No panel computes scores, resolves aliases or decides rules.

nodes.label: Layer dependency direction
nodes.rationale: Imports point downward; core is DOM-free and storage-free; the only outward channel from the engine is the EventBus.

nodes.label: Packet switching and TCP/IP packet contents
nodes.norm_label: packet switching and tcp/ip packet contents
nodes.rationale: Segmenting data into packets that travel independently and are reassembled enhances efficiency and reliability; routers dynamically find alternative routes and a lost packet is re-requested, so the network tolerates issues.

nodes.label: Cache memory
nodes.rationale: Stores frequently used instructions and data in or near the CPU to reduce the time needed to access data from main memory (RAM), speeding up the fetch process; larger and well-levelled caches reduce average memory access time.

nodes.label: Virtual memory
nodes.rationale: Extends the computer's RAM by using part of the hard drive as additional memory so more applications can run simultaneously; overuse causes thrashing where the system spends more time swapping pages than executing instructions.
